title.narrative: Belet Weyne Crisis Response: Securing Food Access through Cash Transfers and Agricultural Inputs for IDPs and At-Risk Households

description.narrative: ltpgtltbrgtBeletWeyne district is experiencing a severe humanitarian crisis marked by escalating food insecurity. Extensive flooding has submerged over 4,990 hectares of farmland, devastating local agriculture. This environmental disaster, coupled with prolonged dry spells, displacement, and soaring food prices, has left many households unable to meet their basic food needs, necessitating urgent humanitarian intervention.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtIn response, the project targets 1,977 vulnerable households, approximately 11,862 individuals including 5,955 internally displaced persons (IDPs), 54% women-headed households, and 480 persons with disabilities. These beneficiaries are distributed across 16 priority locations covering both IDP settlements and host communities. The targeted sites include Alla-bari IDP (4.735474, 45.21123) with 45 HH, Barwaqo IDP (4.73297, 45.21783) with 100 HH, Bilan 2 IDP (4.732117, 45.21687) with 53 HH, Cadani IDP (4.721443, 45.20785) with 85 HH, Daanyeere IDP (4.763151, 45.20432) with 44 HH, Doonsubagle IDP (4.72502, 45.20341) with 80 HH, Ex-Airport IDP (4.739793, 45.19021) with 126 HH, Hadhqaboobe/Lasqudhun IDP (4.76211, 45.20526) with 70 HH, Hiraan Bile (4.78058, 45.23829) with 246 HH, Hodley (4.733223, 45.19819) with 130 HH, Lafole (4.81353, 45.1787) with 290 HH, Najax IDP (4.760706, 45.20741) with 57 HH, Nasib IDP (4.731949, 45.18058) with 270 HH, Nasteex IDP (4.752055, 45.21748) with 160 HH, Qooqane (4.84833, 45.1786) with 130 HH, and Shiilow IDP (4.734962, 45.18072) with 91 HHs, distributed across northern, eastern, and southern parts of the district.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThe intervention is designed to provide lifesaving unconditional cash transfers (UCT) valued at $55 per household per month for three months, totaling $326,205. The UCTs aim to enhance immediate access to food by enabling households to purchase essential items, offering recipients autonomy to address their specific needs while revitalizing local markets.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtIn addition, the project will provide emergency agricultural inputs worth $45 each to 500 vulnerable households with access to arable land. These inputs include climate-resilient, short-cycle seeds to facilitate the production of early-maturing crops, extending food availability beyond the immediate relief phase and improving household dietary diversity. Beneficiaries will also receive training on climate-smart agricultural practices, including soil conservation and water management techniques, aimed at enhancing productivity and building resilience to future environmental shocks.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtBeneficiary selection follows a rigorous vulnerability-based targeting process, prioritizing households facing multiple risk factors such as displacement, female headship, disability, and limited livelihood options. Cash transfers will primarily be delivered through secure mobile money platforms, ensuring safe, timely, and efficient distribution, while alternative mechanisms will be used in areas with limited connectivity.ltbrgtOxfam will leverage its existing programs in Belet Weyne, funded by the Dutch Relief Alliance and AiCS, to integrate this intervention within a broader multi-sectoral framework. Active participation in the Area-Based Coordination (ABC) platform will enhance collaboration with local authoritiesnbsp and humanitarian actors.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThis intervention is fully aligned with the SHF Standard Allocation 1 – 2025 Strategy and the priorities outlined in the Food Security Cluster and the 2025 Humanitarian Response Plan.ltbrgtlt/pgt
